t1: Start with the expected delivery, not the route scans.
Filter delivery_expectations to the row EX-01.
Read the parcel id and the expected contents together.
t2: A receipt describes what the receiver actually observed.
Filter receipts to the row RC-01 and read contents_observed.
Compare the parcel and contents with what EX-01 expected.
t3: Inspect the label changes made before dispatch.
Filter label_audit to field_changed = PARCEL_CODE and order by time.
Compare both parcels’ old and new values: one moves to the other’s code.
t4: The dashboard is built from scan records, not from opening parcels.
Read the note column of the route scans, in time order.
The scanner reads the current label destination and never the contents.
t5: Trace the audit actor, not the person who received the parcel.
Order label_audit by event time and look at actor_id on the PARCEL_CODE rows.
Both code changes name the same actor.
t6: Explain the reciprocal swap, the route result and the calibration-sheet message together.
Join the label audit and route scans, then read the messages sent by the actor.
Do not claim the module was recovered: the records only show its route to the Storage Bay.
